citations.narrative:
Several incidents of minor trauma resulted from inadvertent pairing of incompatible non-human primates in indoor housing
or during escapes while handling monkeys for cage changes. These incidents were reported by the facility to regulatory
agencies prior to inspection.
On 26 March, 2026 an 8 year old female macaque received minor injuries after an altercation with another female that
was unhurt when they were inadvertently paired. On 30 April 2026, a 10 year old female was identified with minor wounds
and and treated by vet staff, at which time it was identified that on or about 28 April 2026 two females were incorrectly pair
housed.
On 1 April 2026, during cage change, the technician inadvertently did not move the required locks from the old rack to the
new rack, which allowed the three macaques housed in that enclosure to open the door and escape into the room. One
animal re-entered the enclosure voluntarily and was secured, the second and third animals were net caught and also
secured. Veterinary exams revealed mild bruising and a nail avulsion on a 9.75 year old female monkey. On 27 April
2026, a 1 year old male macaque escaped the transfer cage during cage cleaning procedures and was hand caught
within 15 minutes with a minor laceration and bruising in the area of the right eye.
Handling of all animals shall be done as expeditiously and carefully as possible in a manner that does not cause trauma
or unnecessary discomfort in order to ensure the welfare of the animals.
Corrected at the time of inspection on 21 July 2026

Primary enclosures must be constructed and maintained so that they protect the non-human primates from injury. These
incidents were reported by the facility to regulatory agencies prior to inspection.
On 16 March 2026, a 3 year old female macaque in an outdoor enclosure was found with her finger caught in the bolt hole
of a climbing structure due to broken PVC pipe that was removed, leaving an opening where the bolt was removed and
not replaced. The traumatic injury was immediately treated by veterinary staff, resulting in a digit amputation on her left
hand.
On 10 March 2026 a 2 year old female macaque was treated for a cheek pouch erosion, and during veterinary treatment
a piece of PVC pipe was removed from her mouth. The small sharp piece of PVC pipe had broken off a section of PVC
covering the chain on a suspended enrichment device in the outdoor housing enclosure.
On 4 February 2026, a group of 4 macaques was noticed to be playing with fastening hardware that had been recently
replaced, but was not secure for standard animal activity resulting in loose material in the enclosure. All animals were
screened for foreign material and one animal passed a small piece of hardware without harm to the animal.
Primary enclosures must be constructed and maintained to protect the non-human primates from injury.
Corrected at the time of inspection on 21 July 2026

Primary enclosures must be constructed and maintained to contain the nonhuman primates securely. This incident was
reported by the facility to regulatory agencies prior to inspection.
On 23 March 2026 a 13 year old male macaque was injured in an altercation with an 11 year old male macaque when the
rivet on a sliding door failed, allowing accidental opening of the pairing door by the animal. The 13 year old male
sustained initial injuries that required surgical repair and subsequent infection resulted in extended treatment and healed
by second intention.
Corrected at the time of inspection on 21 July 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the Veterinary and IACUC staff.
Additional Inspectors:
William Campbell, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
